# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy — Appeal of Denial for Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)**
**Member:** Rowan Carter
**Member ID:** W473677710
**Reference Number:** POC-CD6AF51965-72160
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-10

Dear Molina Healthcare Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my rotator cuff repair surgery (CPT 29827), which my surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented as medically necessary. My claim was denied on 2026-08-10 with the stated reason that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I am asking Molina to reconsider this decision because my medical records show that I did complete conservative treatment, and that treatment did not resolve my symptoms.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

Molina's own policy, *Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy* (https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf), sets out the criteria used to decide whether shoulder arthroscopy is medically necessary. I want to walk through those criteria and show how my records meet them.

**1. Documented loss of function that interferes with daily activities.**

The policy states that shoulder arthroscopy "may be considered medically necessary" when there is:

> " Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

My records document that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. This has been ongoing for 24 months.

**2. Failure of non-surgical management for at least three months, including at least two treatment types.**

The policy states:

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My records show more than three months of non-surgical treatment across multiple types of care:
- NSAIDs for 8 months, with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief;
- Supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 24 visits completed from 2026-05-23 to 2026-07-18.

That is three separate forms of conservative treatment, sustained well beyond three months when the record is considered as a whole, none of which resolved my symptoms.

**3. Functionally limited range of motion on exam.**

The policy also references:

> "and  Demonstration of functionally limited range of motion (active or passive) on physical examination as compared to the non-involved side"

My exam findings document that my range of motion is limited by pain and that provocative testing was positive on the affected side. [Placeholder: if the exam note includes a side-to-side comparison of range of motion, please confirm and attach that portion of the note, as this appeal relies on the record as written.]

## A question about which criteria were actually applied

The denial notice does not specify which category of shoulder arthroscopy criteria in MCP-404 was applied to my rotator cuff repair. The excerpts I have been able to review name categories for diagnostic arthroscopy, debridement, loose body removal, synovectomy, labral repair/biceps tenodesis, distal clavicle excision/decompression, capsulorrhaphy, and capsular release/lysis of adhesions — but I have not seen a category specific to rotator cuff repair for a full-thickness tear, which is what my MRI of 2026-07-06 showed (a 1.8 cm full-thickness supraspinatus tear with grade 2 fatty atrophy). I am asking Molina to identify precisely which written criteria were used to evaluate my request.

Molina's utilization management materials state that the criteria used are MCG guidelines available behind the secure provider portal, and that members may call to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. **I am formally requesting, in writing, the MCG guideline title and criteria applied to my determination**, so that I can understand exactly what standard was used and confirm that my records were measured against it correctly.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Molina to reconsider the denial of my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) in light of the conservative treatment documented in my records, and to provide the specific criteria applied to my case as requested above. I understand this letter does not guarantee that my appeal will be approved, but I believe the record supports a full review.

My appeal must be received by 2027-02-06. I understand Molina's appeal process is administered by state, and I am submitting this appeal through the address printed on my denial notice and/or the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com, as instructed. I can also be reached by phone at the number on my member ID card if additional information is needed.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Rowan Carter
Member ID: W473677710
[Address]
